newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wetlands program to aid Florida lake project.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wetlands program to aid Florida lake project.

text.p: A federal wetlands program will buy 30-year easements on 13,000 acres of land as part of a project to restore Lake Apopka in northern Florida, U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday.
The goal is to restore Lake Apopka, near Orlando, for swimming and fishing.
The easements, for land along the shoreline, will cost about $26 million and will help restore wetlands on the north shore of the lake that were drained during the 1940s.

In a statement, USDA said the wetlands project culminated a long-term restoration program by St Johns River Water Management District. Wetlands restoration is intended to reduce agricultural runoff, principally phosphorus, into the lake.
